input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds only the Customer and is walk-away territory under NOSOLICIT: it is a true no-hire ("hire, or employ"), runs 24 months post-term, covers every Vendor employee rather than only personnel involved in the Services, and expressly overrides any general-advertising or unsolicited-application carve-out ("regardless of how the employee applies"). It also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment. We propose the fallback formulation per the rule's redline guidance: mutual, 12 months from the end of an individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and the no-hire element deleted.

proposal.summary: Narrow one-way 24-month no-hire to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a one-way, 24-month bar on hiring or employing any Vendor employee, including those who apply on their own initiative; our playbook permits at most a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, running 12 months from the end of that involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no no-hire element. This also removes the conflict with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment.

ops.oldText: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: 12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement in the Services, neither party shall knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment activity not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to unsolicited approaches by an individual, and neither party is restricted from hiring or engaging any person who responds to such advertisements or makes such an approach.
